config.title: Notification Context

intro.title: Notification Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification system using React's Context API. You will create a context to manage notification messages across your app, eliminating the need to pass props through many components. The core concept is React Context, which provides a way to share state globally. You'll implement a context provider, a custom hook to use the context, and components to display notifications. This will help you understand how to manage and share state efficiently in a React application.
intro.usecase: Notification contexts are essential in modern web applications where multiple components need to display status updates without prop drilling. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce dashboards showing order confirmations, social media apps displaying new message alerts, and banking applications presenting transaction success/failure messages. Developers implement notification contexts to manage toast messages, banners, and snackbars that appear across different UI sections like headers, modals, or side panels. This centralized approach ensures consistent user feedback while keeping components decoupled and maintainable.

objectives: Construct a React context to manage global notification state.
Initialize the notification context with a default state and a dispatch function.
Implement a context provider component to wrap the application and supply the notification state.
Apply the useContext hook within components to access the notification context.
Manipulate the notification state by dispatching actions to add or remove notifications.
Render dynamic notification components based on the current context state.
Integrate the notification context into existing components to display user feedback.

steps.title: Create NotificationContext using createContext
steps.instruction: Create a context named NotificationContext using React.createContext() with default values of null for both state and setState.
steps.hint: Call createContext from React and assign it to a const variable. Provide an object with state and setState properties as the default value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a context with default values
const UserContext = React.createContext({ user: null, setUser: () => {} });

steps.instruction: Wrap your existing showNotification and hideNotification functions with useCallback to memoize them.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
